rv.q: Never less than abundantly creative, funny and musically dextrous, Kathy and Stella's exploits will absolutely slay you.
Barbé and Hinds are a strong double act with yin-yang energy and impressive vocal ranges.
Happily, while the show has a flaw or two that keeps it just shy of outright excellence, forcible feelgoodery is not among them.
At its best, however, this is still a hugely likeable, self-deprecating piece, bubbling with mischievous energy and carried by two cracking central performances.
But in the more rarefied atmosphere of the West End the constant barrage of gurning and caterwauling is a major turn-off.
This show is an absolute smash-hit and deserves to be nominated for all the awards.
Kathy and A Murder! is the latest heartening new British musical success story.
The show makes few demands of the audience but it has terrific comic integrity and a wonderful sense of fun.
The comedic show is a certified homicidal hoot
Bronté Barbé and Rebekah Hinds as Kathy and Stella respectively have terrific chemistry; their little jokes, cultural references and mannerisms are those of a long term friendship.

There are moments – especially in the songs – that are laugh-out-loud hilarious and that feel freshly observed. And there are other moments that feel a little clunky – like a production struggling to unify its tone.

Because something good is happening when a young group, outside the established and celebrated mainstream, get together and make a show on the fringes, daring to be different, facing the perils of launching it down the slipway to fill the stalls with surprised glee.
It's all good fun, but the comedy is too broad, the songs not sufficiently distinguished, and the crime solving of the title not nearly knotty enough to make it great.
